title: One op at a time
starter:
let apply (op : string) (a : int) (b : int) : int =
  match op with
  | "add" -> a + b
  | "mul" -> 0
  | "max" -> 0
  | _ -> failwith op
hints: Copy the shape of the `add` branch. Only the math changes.
OCaml has a built-in `max a b`. Or write `if a > b then a else b`.

answer.code:
let apply (op : string) (a : int) (b : int) : int =
  match op with
  | "add" -> a + b
  | "mul" -> a * b
  | "max" -> max a b
  | _ -> failwith op
answer.explain: Each op is one branch that turns two numbers into one: `a * b` for `mul` and `max a b` for `max`. An interpreter is mostly a list of branches like these, one per op the language has.
